sections.text:
wallet send: --datum <hex> attaches an inline datum to the recipient output (#37)
Contributed by Ziyang (as exfer-stack) upstream to ahuman-exfer/exfer, the Exfer chain itself.
https://github.com/ahuman-exfer/exfer/pull/39

Implements #37 per the review notes there, plus the PROVISIONAL-note cleanup asked for in the PR #38 sign-off (separate commit).

## The five notes, point by point

- **Recipient output only, never change** — `build_transaction` attaches the datum to the recipient `TxOutput` literal only; the change output is still built datum-free via `TxOutput::new_p2pkh`. A unit test asserts the change output carries neither `datum` nor `datum_hash`.
- **`Option<Vec<u8>>` through `build_transaction`** — new trailing param; the wallet.rs unit-test call sites pass `None` (two additional integration call sites in `tests/audit_fix_tests_33.rs` also pass `None` — mechanical compile requirement).
- **`datum_hash` stays `None`** — `(Some, None)` is the size-only consensus path; no hash is computed anywhere.
- **Enforce `MAX_DATUM_SIZE` + reject bad hex in the CLI, before building** — validation is the first thing the Send handler does, before the passphrase prompt, the signature-domain RPC, and any UTXO work. Bad hex, empty datum (`""` decodes to zero bytes — a present-but-empty wire form nobody means from a flag; rejected rather than attached silently), and oversize all fail with a clean message and provably zero RPC traffic (the CLI tests assert the mock node saw no methods). Oversize wording mirrors walletd: `datum is N bytes, exceeds MAX_DATUM_SIZE 4096`.
- **Generic `--datum <hex>`** — the base wallet knows nothing about EXFER-QUOTE; quote-binding stays the caller's convention. The string appears nowhere in the change (fixtures use neutral bytes).
- **Echo** — the attached datum is echoed as canonical lowercase hex in both JSON objects (`"datum"` field, only when present) and both human paths (`Datum:` line).

## Tests

One note-level addition: the #37 comment cites the coinbase-output validation path (`validation.rs:216-226`); wallet-built transactions actually traverse the tx-level pass (`validation.rs:387-393` with the both-present guard at `427-431`). A consensus test pins the boundary through that exact path: a wallet-built `(Some, None)` transaction validates at 4096 bytes and fails `DatumOversized` at 4097. No consensus code touched.

## Verified on a live devnet node

`send --to xfd1... --datum 00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff` (a 16-byte quote_id-shaped payload, bech32m recipient — doubles as a #38 regression check): confirmed next block, datum readable on-chain via `get_transaction`, `datum_hash` absent, recipient balance credited. A full 4096-byte datum built, submitted, and confirmed through real consensus. All three rejections exercised at the CLI layer with nonzero exits and no node traffic.

One observation, no change made: the deser-cost comment at `consensus/cost.rs:72` ("In Phase 1, datums are always None") is now stale — datum bytes were already priced (`ceil(len/64)` per output); this change just makes the case reachable from the CLI. Left untouched as consensus territory.

Closes #37.
